title: Finite sets of points of a locally algebraic group have a common affine open
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $H$ be a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every integer $n\geq0$ and every list of $k$-morphisms $h_1,\ldots,h_n:\operatorname{Spec}k\to H$, there exists an affine open subscheme $U\subseteq H$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] through which all the $h_i$ factor. The points need not be distinct, and $H$ need not be quasi-compact, connected, smooth or reduced.

source.place: Tag 0B7S (lemma-points-in-affine); locally algebraic means locally of finite type over the field.

proof.text: Put $C=H^0$. The identity-component theorem applies since $k$ is algebraically closed and $H/k$ is locally of finite type: $C$ is a clopen irreducible open subgroup scheme. For each connected component $D$ met by a marked point choose one such point $a\in H(k)$. Left translation $L_a$ is a scheme isomorphism with inverse $L_{a^{-1}}$. It maps $C$ onto $D$: its image is connected and contains $a$, and the inverse image of the connected component $D$ is connected and contains the identity; maximality of the two connected components gives both inclusions. Thus $D$ is clopen and $L_a$ identifies its open-subscheme structure with $C$. Restricting the two inverse maps through the open subschemes is legitimate by the open-factorization lemma. Only finitely many components are met, since there are only $n$ indices; no finiteness assertion about all components of $H$ is needed.

Fix one of these components and its chosen $a$. Translate its marked points to $b_i=a^{-1}h_i\in C(k)$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V$ of the identity in the scheme $C$ (the local affine neighbourhood in the definition of a scheme). For each of these indices put $O_i=R_{b_i^{-1}}(V)\subset C$. Right translation and its inverse preserve $C$, since $C$ is a subgroup; the open-factorization lemma restricts them to inverse isomorphisms of $C$. Hence each $O_i$ is nonempty and open. Their finite intersection $O$ is nonempty: in an irreducible space two nonempty opens meet, since otherwise their proper closed complements cover the space; induction gives the finite-intersection assertion. This uses irreducibility of the underlying space only and does not replace $C$ by its reduction.

source.place: Tag 0B7S (lemma-points-in-affine), intersection of translated affine opens

proof.text: Because $C/k$ is of finite type, it is locally of finite type. Apply the Jacobson-space statement with the closed subset $Z=C$: closed points of $C$ are dense, so the nonempty open $O$ contains a closed point $x$. The closed-residue-field statement applies with the same algebraically closed $k$ and locally finite type $C$; it says that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an isomorphism. Compose its inverse with the residue point $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to C$ to obtain a $k$-rational point $g\in O(k)$. This justifies the rational point required in the intersection without assuming that $O$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson); morphisms.tex Tag 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points); groupoids.tex Tag 0B7S rational-point choice

proof.text: For each index in the chosen component, $g\in R_{b_i^{-1}}(V)$ implies $gb_i\in V$, by applying the inverse translation $R_{b_i}$. Consequently $b_i\in L_{g^{-1}}(V)$. Translation is an isomorphism, so $L_{g^{-1}}(V)$ is affine and open in $C$. Translate back by $a$: $U_D=L_aL_{g^{-1}}(V)$ is an affine open in $D$ and hence in $H$, and contains all marked points in $D$. The order of the products is as written: no commutativity of $H$ is being used.

Take $U=\bigcup_D U_D$ over the finitely many components met by the list. These opens are pairwise disjoint. Each $U_D$ is also closed in $U$, since its complement is the union of the other opens. Its open inclusion into $U$ is a closed immersion: its map of structure sheaves is the identity on stalks in $U_D$ and has zero target stalks off $U_D$, hence is surjective, and its underlying image is closed. Thus the affine closed subschemes $U_D$ cover $U$, and the closed-affine-union theorem proves $U$ affine. Every $h_i$ factors uniquely through $U$ by the open-factorization lemma. For $n=0$ take $U=\varnothing=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$; the factorization condition is vacuous. Repeated points affect none of the argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q143-363d89537 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 0B7S (lemma-points-in-affine, l.1329-1362) and the identity-component node (0B7R). The statement is byte-identical to live, where the item was unsplit with an empty proof, so this is a first split, not a re-split. No new nodes, no SGA. The 5 steps follow the source: (1) G^0 is clopen, an irreducible finite-type subgroup, and L_a maps C onto each component D that a marked point meets (both inclusions by maximality of components); (2) an affine V at e and the nonempty opens O_i = R_{b_i^{-1}}(V) of irreducible C meet (elementary, topological only, valid for nonreduced C); (3) the Jacobson node with Z=C and the Nullstellensatz residue node give g in C(k) inside O; (4) b_i in L_{g^{-1}}V and h_i in U_D = L_a L_{g^{-1}}V, product order checked, no commutativity used; (5) U_D are disjoint and clopen, the open inclusion is a closed immersion by the stalk check, and 09NL gives U affine; n=0 gives Spec 0. Every cited statement says what its step takes from it. Hypotheses used: only k algebraically closed and locally of finite type. Edge cases checked: n=0, repeated points, constant Z, alpha_p/mu_p, an abelian variety, a nonabelian disconnected group. Duplicate search: rg -L for 0B7S hits only the item and its citer locally-separated-group-space-scheme, whose use matches the statement; 09NM componentwise-finite-set needs finitely many components and is not a duplicate. The five generic tool_uses are accepted.
